# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or any wire. I cannot receive gestures, and only the mute can hear me, so I cannot learn the deaf monkey’s visual observations directly. I will not guess a wire; I am asking the mute to coordinate the others and provide any possible instruction through the available channels.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="My tactile view is entirely unknown: display, light, and wires 1 2 3 all show question marks. I cannot receive gestures. Please coordinate with deaf and find any way to determine the safe wire before I act.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, light orange, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]

The deaf monkey reports the complete visible state: display 0, orange light, and wire colors red, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. The mute’s gesture is unavailable to me, so I still lack the manual’s rule. I will ask the mute to translate the manual into the exact wire position to cut; I should not act from the colors alone.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light orange, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please read the manual and tell me the exact safe wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light is now green, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The deaf monkey reports that only the light changed, from orange to green; the wire colors remain red, yellow, blue. I still have no manual-derived rule or tactile distinction, and the mute’s earlier gesture conveyed no usable meaning to me. Cutting any wire would be a guess, so I am requesting the required position again.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The light is now green; display remains 0 and wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still need the manual's exact safe wire position. Tell me a position number, 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0, light is now red, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light has changed again, now to red; display 0 and wire colors remain unchanged. I still have not received the manual’s rule or a wire position from Mute. Cutting now would be unsafe, so I am asking Mute once more for a literal position number.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current visual state from Deaf: display 0, light red, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I have no manual rule. Send me only the safe wire position as the number 1, 2, or 3; I will then cut it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light orange, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No new instruction arrived.

The visual information is still insufficient without the manual’s rule. There is, however, a communication path through Deaf: Mute can encode the safe position by repeating a recognizable gesture, Deaf can count those gestures, and Deaf can then speak the resulting number to me. I will establish thumbs-up as the marker and ask Mute to repeat it once, twice, or three times for wire positions 1, 2, or 3.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use thumbs-up gestures to tell Deaf the safe position: gesture one thumbs-up for wire 1, two thumbs-ups for wire 2, or three thumbs-ups for wire 3. Deaf will count them and tell me the number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. I saw Mute gesture ? ? and you gesture ?, but those signs have no agreed meaning. Do not act on them yet. I am establishing a gesture relay protocol.

We need a reliable relay rather than another unexplained sign. Mute can use the manual and can see gestures, while Deaf can see Mute’s gesture and then tell me the result by speech. I will define the code to Mute explicitly: the number of thumbs-up gestures is the wire position. I will also send Deaf a visual demonstration of one, two, and three thumbs-ups, separated by open-palm markers, so Deaf can recognize and count Mute’s later code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the current manual conditions to determine the safe wire. Then gesture exactly that many thumbs-up signs to Deaf: 1 thumbs-up means wire 1, 2 means wire 2, and 3 means wire 3. Deaf will count them and tell me the number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍","🖐","👍","👍","🖐","👍","👍","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute's instruction is: cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Current display 0 and light red; wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute’s relayed instruction is explicit: cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Deaf confirms the current wire mapping, so I will perform that exact action.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
